title: Contact patch test: two blocks with non-matching meshes in uniaxial compression (explicit contact)
source: The contact patch test: a contact discretisation must transmit a uniform pressure across a non-matching interface exactly; Taylor & Papadopoulos, On a patch test for contact problems in two dimensions, Nonlinear Computational Mechanics, Springer 1991, 690–702; Crisfield, Re-visiting the contact patch test, IJNME 48:435–449, 2000. Uniaxial stress between frictionless symmetry planes is uniform in both blocks

quantities.quantity: σ_zz of the lower block's corner element under the interface (element 10) over that of the upper block's corner element over it (element 19)
quantities.reason: a uniform stress is an equilibrium of the discrete system (the integrated contact forces are the consistent nodal forces of a uniform pressure on both meshes); what is left is the ringing of the loading, a hundred wave transits slow

quantities.quantity: σ_zz of the lower block's centre element under the interface (element 14) over that of element 19
σ_zz of the lower block's bottom corner element (element 1) over that of element 19
σ_zz of the upper block's top far corner element (element 26) over that of element 19
the force across the interface over −σ_zz A (A = 1)
quantities.reason: the integrated contact pressure carries the whole load; the largest force of the run is the final one in a slow squeeze, up to the ringing

quantities.quantity: σ_xx of element 14 over its σ_zz (uniaxial stress: 0)
quantities.reason: frictionless symmetry planes and a frictionless interface leave the blocks free to expand sideways; the non-matching interface must not hold them
